Heavy snow fell throughout Union County during the duration of the storm. The COOP observer in Maynardville recorded an event total of 9 inches of snow. Additionally, a trained spotter south of Maynardville recorded 8.3 inches of snow with a fine glaze of ice, and another spotter measured 6.4 inches of snow in Sharps Chapel.
Snow amounts around 6 to 7 inches were reported near Maynardville and Sharps Chapel.
Near Maynardville, 3 inches of snow was estimated.
A weather station outside of Citico recorded a 62 mph non-thunderstorm wind gust.
A public weather station recorded a 63 mph non-thunderstorm wind gust southeast of Citico, Tennessee.
Near Citico, 5.8 inches of snow was reported.
Light snow fell in Marion County, with a CoCoRaHS observer in Jasper measuring 1.6 inches of snow and the county Emergency Manager measuring 1.2 inches of snow in South Pittsburg.

A major winter storm brought heavy snow and a light glaze of ice to Marion County, with snowfall reports from public, the EM, and CoCoRaHS of 4.5 inches in Jasper, 5 inches in Lone Oak, 4 inches in Whitwell, almost 3 inches in Tracy City, and 5 inches in South Pittsburg.

A primarily heavy snow event covered Marion County, with periods of sleet, freezing rain, and rain falling during brief mixed precipitation periods during the storm. A COOP observer in Whitwell measured 6 inches of snow, a CoCoRaHS observer outside of Whitwell reported a snow total of 4.2 inches and an unknown amount of freezing rain and sleet resulting in a heavy glaze on top of the snowpack.
Near Monteagle, 4 inches of snow was reported.

Light snow fell in Hamblen County, the official two day total from NWS Morristown is 2.1 inches of snow. Additionally Morristown Radio recorded 1.6 inches of snow and a member of the public measured 1.6 inches of snow in Talbott.

Snow began in the early afternoon, generally small flakes. Then between 5 and 630 was a period of light sleet/freezing rain mix, snow then came in and light snow continued until  gradually lessening and stopping before 11 PM. Measured total was 2.3 inches of snow with a SWE of 0.28.
Official snowfall measurement of 0.6 inches as measured at the NWS Morristown WFO.

A high wind event from Helene felled roughly 100 trees within Panther Creek State Park, leading to multiple trail closures. A few swaths of trees down were observed, with one swath estimated to be over 100 yards long. At 8:10 AM LST, a 52 mph wind gust was measured at Morristown Airport, matching time when the western half of the city lost power, including the Morristown WFO. At 9:05 AM LST, Hamblen County headquarters measured a 45 mph wind gust. Most of Panther Creek Park's wind damage occurred at higher elevations within the park.

Steady rain and freezing rain observed between roughly 9:30 PM and 11:00 PM, with a mix of freezing rain, sleet, and occasional snow observed between 11:00 PM and Midnight. Had transitioned back to freezing drizzle at observation time.|Snowfall attributed to sleet accumulation. Total snow and sleet accumulation around 0.1. Also measured 0.04 of ice accretion on trees and other objects around the office. Precipitation came to an end overnight, then a light snow fell during the day, resulting in an additional 1.5 inches of snowfall at the office.

An official event total of 8.6 inches of snow was measured at the Morristown WFO. Very brief periods of sleet mixed in, but the bulk of the event was all snow. Also measured was a 9 inch CoCoRaHS report on the Hamblen and Jefferson County lines. A Facebook report of 9 inches of snow was recorded near Alpha, TN. 6 inches of snow fell in Lowland, TN.

Two bouts of snow led to heavy snowfall in northwest Carter County, with a Shady Valley Facebook report of 4.5 inches with heavy snowfall at time of report being relayed. Elsewhere, 2.5 inches of snow was measured near Milligan College.

Midday snow followed by snow bands in the afternoon led to at the least light snow in Sadie, where 3 inches of snow was measured during a passage of a moderate snow band. While it's likely Sadie saw additional snowfall, additional reports are unavailable.
Snow fell across Carter County, with 4 inches of snow measured by the public in Sadie. The COOP observer in Elizabethton recorded 2.5 inches of snow.
A light snow event resulted in 2 inches of snow measured in Sadie, and the CO-OP observer in Elizabethton reported 0.8 inches of snowfall.

A Facebook county feed reported that a golf course in Elizabethton received significant tree damage from Helene's winds. Additionally several trees were felled along Smalling Road, Constitution Avenue, and several other roads across the county.

A mix of heavy precipitation types occurred across Carter County, with the northern stretches receiving mostly snow, and southwestern portions having a wintry mix. The COOP observer in Elizabethton recorded an inch of snow, but a public report near Sadie received 7.8 inches of snow.
Severe drought conditions during September 2025 improved to moderate drought in early October across Humphreys County. By the end of the month, no drought conditions were present across the county.
Severe drought conditions developed across northern Humphreys County during September 2025.
A weather station in New Johnsonville recorded a maximum heat index of 114 degrees.
A resident near McEwen reported an estimated 3 inches of snow.
A CoCoRaHS observer near McEwen measured 3.4 inches of snow. Heavy snow across Humphreys County resulted in difficult driving conditions.
Severe drought conditions from September 2024 improved in October with abnormally dry conditions across Humphreys County.

costliest.narrative: Several hours of severe non-thunderstorm winds resulted in numerous reports of downed and uprooted trees, downed powerlines, and roof and other property damage across all of Humphreys County. Tragically, this event was responsible for one fatality and one injury in Humphreys County. A tree fell near the intersection of Little Blue Creek Road and East Blue Creek Road between McEwen and Waverly. The tree fell on a car, impaling and killing 62-year-old James Howard Warner who was driving. The man's nephew, who was a passenger in the car, was injured and hospitalized. Damages are estimated.

A brushfire was started near Cuba Landing Road in Waverly around 4:32 PM. When Humphreys County firefighters arrived on scene, they found that the fire had spread to engulf two homes and two sheds. The two homes and one shed were completely destroyed, but firefighters were able to salvage the other shed. Five acres were burned before the fire was extinguished around midnight. No injuries were reported. The cause of the fire is under investigation. Damages are estimated.

This is a continuation of the event that began at the end of January 2023. Ice accumulations in Humphreys County forced the closure of Interstate 40 eastbound between the Tennessee River and Highway 13. A multi-car pileup blocked the roadway, but no information was available on any potential injuries. Damages are a rough estimate.

recent.narrative: A cold front sparked widespread showers, with one notable thunderstorm rapidly traversing the Tennessee Valley, producing hail up to 1 inch.

An EF0 tornado touched down in southern Loudon County in the early morning hours with max winds of 85 mph. Tornado was in Loudon County for roughly 1 mile before exiting into northern Monroe County east of Holt Road. Several injuries occurred when either the tornado itself or the rear flank downdraft winds rolled a camper RV several times up and over a wooden service post. In addition to the RV on the south side of the damage swath, several trees suffered damage, there was roof damage to small structures and a barn, and the tornado left cycloidal markings in the field beyond the RV and houses. When the tornado reached the tree line at the edge of Loudon, several trees had large branches broken off.
Multiple trees were blown down by powerful thunderstorm winds.
Multiple reports of trees being blown down by severe thunderstorm gusts across the county. Additionally utility data showed over 1,000 customers were without power.
County dispatchers reported several trees across the county were blown down by severe thunderstorm winds.
Multiple trees were blown down in and around Loudon by severe thunderstorm wind gusts.

costliest.narrative: Loudon County High sustained significant roof damage to the gymnasium. The roof decking was ripped off the building. The only other structural damage on site was to the ticket booth, which also had the roof lifted off and destroyed.

recent.narrative: Light snow was recorded across Anderson County, with CoCoRaHS observers reporting 1.6 inches of snow in Norris, 1.1 inches and 1.2 inches of snow in Oak Ridge. Additionally the public reported 1.2 inches of snow in Oak Ridge.

Heavy snow fell across the southern portions of Anderson County, with lighter snowfall in the northern half of the county. Sleet and wintry mix mixed in at times in Anderson, a report near Briceville indicated .05 of freezing rain had occurred. The highest reports were observed by CoCoRaHS volunteers, including 4 inches in Oak Ridge, 3 inches east of Oak Ridge, 2.8 inches in Norris, and 2.5 inches of snow in Heiskell.

Heavy snowfall fell across Anderson County, with a maximum of 11 inches reported in Oak Ridge. Other reports include: 10 inches reported by the public in Clinton, 8.5 inches from a CoCoRaHS observer in Norris, 8 inches in Heiskell from a public report, 8 inches in Andersonville from a public report, amongst others.
A wind gust to 46 mph was measured at the KOQT ASOS.
A wind gust to 45 mph was measured at the KMNV AWOS.
Snow amounts between 4 and 7 inches were reported across the county.
A strong non-thunderstorm gust of wind felled a large pine tree in Cleveland, TN, with the tree landing on a carport.
Light snow fell in a brief burst in Bradley, leading to 2 inches of snow in Cleveland, 2 inches in Charleston, and 1 inch in Tasso.
A large tree was blown down by synoptic winds onto a house.

Heavy snow fell during the middle portions of the day in Bradley County, before transitioning to sleet, then freezing rain, then eventually to rain to end the event. The highest snowfall report was 5.5 inches from a spotter in Cleveland. Other reports included 4 inches in Charleston, 3.5 inches in Waterville, 4.5 inches in Tasso, and 3.5 inches with a glaze of ice in Gap Springs.

A trained spotter reported an event total of 4 inches of snowfall in Georgetown, TN. Another spotter reported 3 inches of snow in Charleston, TN. A CoCoRaHS report of 2 inches was received from Cleveland, TN.
The wind gust was measured at the airport (KRZR).

costliest.narrative: A strong non-thunderstorm gust of wind felled a large pine tree in Cleveland, TN, with the tree landing on a carport.

recent.narrative: Two bursts of snow led to 3.2 inches of snowfall in Newport per an image relayed by media. The CO-OP observer in Newport measured 1.5 inches of snow.
Heavy snow fell on top of English Mountain, social media report at 2500 feet reported 4 to 6 inches of snow on the mountain, with the roads snow and ice covered.

Snow, likely interrupted at times with wintry mix, led to heavy snow reports in Cocke County. All reports were received on Facebook: 5.5 inches of snow in Newport, 3 inches in Cosby, and 3 inches of snow in Del Rio.
Numerous trees were felled by Helene's prolonged high wind event, causing over 4,000 customers to be without power at the height of the storm per the local utility company.

Precipitation fell mainly as rain in Cocke County for a significant portion of the event, but freezing rain and light snow combined to make transportation extremely hazardous, with the county emergency manager reporting extremely icy roads that were near impassable with several wrecks including tractor trailers.
Near Parrottsville, 4 inches of snow was reported. Near Newport, 7 inches was reported.
A light snow fell across Grainger County, with an observer along Cherokee Lake in Rutledge reporting 1.5 inches of snow.

Light snow and a wintry mix at times fell in Grainger County. Highest report was a CoCoRaHS report of 2.5 inches of snow outside of Rutledge. Another public report of 2 inches of snow in Washburn was also received.

A Facebook report and picture of a two foot diameter, 70 foot tall pine tree uprooted by Helene's winds near Bean Station, TN. A local county newspaper reported 45 electric utility poles and transformers were damaged by the prolonged windstorm, along with over 4500 customers without power. Trees felled by the winds were reported across the county, with some reported damage to homes and outbuildings.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported a quarter inch of snow, sleet, and freezing rain, with light snow at time of measurement.
A public report on Facebook of 10 inches was received from Blaine, TN. Additionally a public report from Washburn measured 8.5 inches of snowfall.
Near Rutledge, 4 inches was reported.
Light snow fell in Kyle's Ford, with the public reporting 2 inches of snowfall.
Light snow fell across Hancock County, with 2.5 inches of snow measured in Sneedville and 1.5 inches of snow measured in Kyles Ford.
A light snow fell across Hancock County, with 2.4 inches of snow measured in Kyles Ford.
A half inch of snow fell near Sneedville and Kyle's Ford.
Light snow event yielded 1.1 inches of snow as measured in Kyles Ford.

Scattered trees were blown down by Helene's winds across the county, resulting in power outages affecting at least one-quarter of the county residents. Additionally, one large tree was felled in the backyard of a private residence in Sneedville, TN.
A few heavy snow squalls were reported near Okolona, the bulk of the 1 inch snowfall was measured between 430 and 530 pm LST.

Light snow fell across Hawkins County, with 3.6 inches of snow measured in Church Hill, 2 inches of snow in Mount Carmel, 2 inches of snow in Surgoinsville, 2 inches in Mooresburg, and 2 inches of snow in Rogersville.

Light to heavy snow fell across Hawkins County, with 4 inches of snow reported by a CoCoRaHS observer in Church Hill, 4 inches of snow reported by the public in Mooresburg, and 2 inches of snow measured by a trained spotter in Surgoinsville.

A light snowfall transitioned to light freezing rain across Hawkins County. In Church Hill, at least 0.6 inches of snow was reported, along with a glaze of ice from sleet and freezing rain. In Okolona, a trained spotter reported an event total of 1.5 inches of snow along with a glaze of ice on numerous outdoor surfaces, resulting in snow and ice covered roadways.
A light snow event resulted in 0.6 inches of snow in Church Hill, 0.5 inches of snow in Surgoinsville, and 0.3 inches of snow in Bulls Gap.

Trees were felled or snapped by high, prolonged winds from Helene across Hawkins County, including several in the Rogersville area, Church Hill, Mount Carmel, and onto 11W and other area roadways. Additionally, the county emergency manager reported several hundred calls for service from wind damage to both trees and powerlines across the county through the storm.

Light snow fell across Knox County. CoCoRaHS reports of snowfall were: 2.6 inches in Knoxville, 1.5 inches in Knoxville, 1 inch in Seymour, 2 inches in Knoxville, 1.7 inches in Karns, and 2 inches in Farragut.

Snow fell in a couple of bursts over Knox County, with wintry mix falling between roughly 1630 EST and 1900 EST based off reports from a trained spotter and the official airport station just south of Knox County. A light glaze of freezing rain was reported by a trained spotter during this event, less than .05. As far as snowfall, 3 to 4 inches of snow was observed in Karns, Farragut, Halls, Powell, Bearden, Maloneyville, and Forest Lake. A NWS employee reported a final total of 2.4 inches near Paulette.

For a several hour period, Knoxville McGhee Tyson ASOS recorded wind gusts above 40 mph. The peak wind gust was recorded at 51 mph at 12:49 PM. These winds, combined with saturated soils, led to multiple reports of tree damage across both Blount and Knox counties, with trees falling on powerlines, blocking roads, and a couple onto cars. Neighboring counties also reported strong gusts, with several 40 to 45 mph gusts recorded in Knox County, and a pair of 40 to 45 mph gusts in neighboring Sevier County. Additionally, the AWOS in Oneida recorded a 51 mph gust at 12:15 PM and the TRI ASOS recorded a 51 mph gust at 4:10 PM.

Light snow fell across Knox County with the highest report from a NWS Employee of 1.2 inches of snow along Sharps Ridge. Other reports included 1.2 inches in downtown Knoxville, 1 inch in Halls, and 0.5 inches in Lake Forest.

Approximately 100 calls were logged by the Knox 911 dispatch for fallen trees during the Helene high wind event. This resulted in numerous trees blocking roads, downing powerlines, and causing thousands of power outages across the county. Several trees were reported down on Warrior Trail as well. A peak wind gust of 49 mph was measured by Knoxville McGhee Tyson Airport at 3:32 PM LST.

Rain, freezing rain, and snow fell with a half inch of snow measured in the Hardin Valley area of Knoxville. Extreme cold followed, with refreezing of roads each night of snowmelt causing additional road hazards.

Light snow fell in Loudon, a CoCoRaHS observer in Loudon measured 2.7 inches of snow. The COOP observer for Lenoir City Utilities measured 2.5 inches of snow. Additional reports were 1.8 inches of snow in Lenoir City, 2 inches in Loudon, and 1.8 inches of snow north of Lenoir City.

Heavy snow fell across Loudon County during the day, before transitioning to a wintry mix and ending late at night. Reported snow amounts include a CoCoRaHS report of 4.3 inches of snow east of Loudon, 4 inches of snow in Lenoir City, 3 inches of snow elsewhere in Lenoir City, and 4.5 inches of snow by the COOP observer in Lenoir City.

Heavy snow fell across Loudon County, with 9 inches reported by a trained spotter in Lenoir City, another spotter nearby reported 8 inches in Lenoir City. A CoCoRaHS observer in Loudon reported an event total 8.5 inches of snow. The Lenoir City COOP observer reported a storm total of 11.8 inches of snowfall.
Snow amounts around 6 to 7 inches were reported around Lenoir City.

Light snow fell in Meigs County, a CoCoRaHS observer in Decatur reported 2.5 inches of snow, another in Ten Mile reported 2 inches of snow. The COOP observer in Decatur reported 2 inches of snow and light ice pellets. Finally a member of the public in Ten Mile reported 2.2 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell across the county during the day, before transitioning to wintry mix and eventually ending in the evening. A report from Ten Mile covered the storm perfectly: Heavy snow totaled 5.5 inches measured at 3:10 PM when wintry mix began. Last couple hours before 3 PM were the heaviest snowfall rates passing 1 inch per hour. As of 6:05 additional sleet and freezing rain have led the snow to compact to 4 inches with a glaze of ice on top of everything. Temperatures have remained in the 20s during the wintry mix.

Heavy snow impacted Meigs County, with a CoCoRaHS observer reported an event total of 10.3 inches of snow near Decatur. The COOP observer in Decatur recorded 7.5 inches of snowfall, and a public report of 6.5 inches was also measured. In Ten Mile, a public report measured 9 inches of snow.
Multiple trees were blown down across the county by powerful non-thunderstorm winds.
Snow amounts of 5 to 6 inches were reported across the county.
Light snow fell in a short period during the morning, leading to an inch of snow in Benton.

Neighboring counties reported heavy snowfall during the daytime hours, however only 1 report of snow was received at 1030 AM EST from Polk County, 1.3 inches of snow south of Etowah TN just across the county line.
Snow amounts of 3 to 4 inches were reported across the county.
Light snow fell in Roane County, the COOP observer in Kingston measured 2 inches of snow, and a CoCoRaHS observer east of Kingston measured 0.5 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell in Roane County, primarily across the southern half of the county, with lesser snowfall amounts in northern Roane. Still, a CoCoRaHS observer in Kingston reported 4 inches of snow, a public report in Kingston reported 3.5 inches, but the CO-OP observer noted only 2.5 inches of snow along with light sleet.

Light freezing rain was noted by the COOP observer in Kingston, but otherwise widespread heavy snow fell across the county. Kingston COOP reported 9 inches of snow, and public reports of 7 inches and 8.5 inches were measured in Eagle Furnace and near Oak Ridge, respectively.

Strong winds blew the roof off a dugout at Rockwood Baseball Complex. The roof fell onto two people, a female adult and a child. Both were transported to local hospitals, where the adult died from her injuries.
A wind chill of -15 F was measured at the Rockwood airport.
Snow amounts of 5 to 7.5 inches were reported across the county.

Light snow fell across most of the North Sevier zone, except for a report of 3 inches of snow just north of Gatlinburg. Otherwise a NWS Employee in Strawberry Plains reported 1.9 inches of snow on the 19th, a spotter in Kodak reported 1.4 inches of snow, and amateur radio reported 1.5 inches of snow in Dollywood and Wears Valley.
At 10 AM a photo was received of a collapsed pavilion near Kodak. An hour prior, the AWOS at KGKT measured a synoptic wind gust of 55 mph.

Light snow in lower elevations of northern Sevier County, most locations reported 2 inches of snow between Sevierville and Pigeon Forge. The highest report of 4 inches of snow came from a location outside of Pigeon Forge on one of the local knobs, at a higher elevation than the valley floor.

Two bouts of snow with wintry mix in between fell across Sevier County, resulting in heavy snowfall and a light glaze of ice on surfaces. The public reported 5 inches of snow in Sevierville, 4 inches of snow in Seymour, 4 inches of snow in Harrisburg, 3.5 inches of snow and sleet in Pigeon Forge, and an NWS Employee reported 3.3 inches of snow and ice near Strawberry Plains.

A sharp gradient of precipitation types existed across Sevier County, with the northernmost portions of the county remaining all snow, while the central portion had mixed precipitation, and the southeastern portions of the zone reported more rain and freezing rain before ending in snow. An off duty NWS Employee reported an event total of 9 inches of snow in Strawberry Plains. A member of the public reported 6 inches in Kodak, and the COOP observer in Sevierville measured 1.5 inches of snow.
Snow amounts of 2 to 4 inches were reported across the county.

Two bouts of snow led to light snowfall accumulations across Sullivan County. A CoCoRaHS observer recorded 3.5 inches of snow near Oak Grove, another CoCoRaHS observer reported 2 inches of snow in Blountville, the public reported 3 inches of snow near South Holston Dam, 3 inches of snow near Bluff City, a trained spotter reported 2 inches of snow near Kingsport, and another trained spotter reported 2 inches of snow and a light glaze of ice in Colonial Heights.

Morning snow followed by afternoon and evening snow bands led to light snow accumulations across Sullivan. Social media reports included 2.5 inches of snow and 3 inches of snow near South Holston Dam, and 1.5 inches of snow in Bristol.

Light snow interrupted at times by wintry mix fell across Sullivan County, with a trained spotter near Bristol reporting a light glaze of ice along with 3.2 inches of snow. Kingsport and Blountville both reported 2 inches of snow, and Gray received 1.6 inches of snow.

A light snow that began in the morning transitioned to wintry mix by the early afternoon before entering a lull until the evening hours. Highest snowfall report was 1.2 inches in Bristol with a light glaze of ice. 0.9 inches of snow was reported in Bluff City, 0.5 inches of snow in Kingsport, and an inch of snow in Blountville. Wintry mix during the evening resulted in an additional light glaze of ice measured in Bristol.

The KTRI Tri-Cities Regional Airport ASOS recorded a 58 mph non-thunderstorm wind gust. An hour prior, wind gusts in the upper 40s were recorded at the airport at the same time reports were received of damage to unknown outdoor objects and smaller tree branches being broken by the gusts. Wind gusts above 40 mph were recorded in multiple counties across the area, including: Washington, Sevier, Knox, Polk, Blount, McMinn, Monroe, Campbell, and Hamilton.
One inch of snowfall fell in Bristol.
Strong diurnal heating but a lack of upper level support led to isolated severe thunderstorms producing large hail in the rural elevated terrain.

Flooding along portions of Hwy 19 was reported at 8:00 am EST. Reports from spotters, social media, broadcast media, and county officials increased through the day, including flooded roadways at 8:51 am EST. Flooding of the Nolichucky River at the Jackson Love Hwy bridge area was noted at 9:32 am EST. Flooding of the grounds around Unicoi Hospital was happening around 10:00 am EST, when a berm was overtopped or breached. The hospital structure was taking water by 11:00 am EST, and evacuation by ground had become unsafe. Occupants were taken to the roof, but winds prevented air rescue while rapidly rising and turbulent river flooding prevented water rescue. The hospital was surrounded and inundated by waters at least 7 feet deep by 12:45 pm EST.
